ai.description: *Hemidactylus platyurus* reaches 10–12 cm. It is translucent grey-brown with dark mottling and possesses a flattened, fringed tail and fully webbed toes. It belongs to the family Gekkonidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Hemidactylus platyurus* is the presence of a distinct, thin, flattened tail with serrated lateral edges, lacking the tubercles found in other *Hemidactylus* species.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus platyurus* typically inhabits tropical moist deciduous forests and human dwellings, ranging from sea level up to approximately 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Flat-tailed House Gecko is primarily nocturnal, often congregating near artificial lights to ambush insects attracted to the glow.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus platyurus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs year-round, peaking during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus platyurus* is found across the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the Northeast, Western Ghats, and coastal regions, ranging from sea level to 1,200 meters.
